method: Read maintained/frozen connector, independent Snell oracle, proposal and native saved-path plan. Rehash every declared input/artifact. Independently verify every saved branch using Fraction arithmetic and read back saved time/momentum errors. No controls, ray traces, native connector calculations or optimizations rerun.
mathematical_findings: For a positive affine speed gradient, R >= sqrt(A)+sqrt(C) is exactly equivalent to left>=0 and left^2>=4AC; the one-leg/two-leg transition decisions preserve the supplied binary64 inputs.
The guide action is R/vB plus sum[(atanh(q)-q)/g], and its endpoint momenta have the correct depth signs. The rationalized guide-length expression equals R-sqrt(A)-sqrt(C).
The admissible interior action 2/g asinh(gD/(2sqrt(va*vb))) differentiates to the two saved endpoint vectors; the stable excess is an algebraic rearrangement of that same action.
The Snell-leg logarithmic oracle and endpoint momenta use a different evaluation formula. Its finite-bottom containment and horizontal monotonicity support the invented finite boxes.
The homogeneous oblique and positive-gradient nonguide cases refute blanket zeroing of a bottom source derivative. Changing only the derivative of the old straight element is correctly rejected.
scope_limits: The 1e-32 km finite differences perturb the 80-digit continuous Snell action, not a binary64 production ray.
Recorded Decimal checks are independent numerical consistency, not outward interval proofs or arbitrary-scale robustness guarantees.
No native computation is approved by this review. The proposed fixed saved-path component must retain the exact grid-derived affine ratio and full source/first-vertex variation.
No full nodal-grid Jacobian, general trilinear-medium connector, optimized whole-path envelope derivative, stationarity or first-arrival certificate follows.
